map.写文案、注释、社交内容时想快速插入 emoji？输入中文或英文关键词（如“笑”“: Need to drop an emoji into copy, a comment or a social post? Type a keyword in English or Chinese (such as "laugh", "fire" or "heart") and click to copy it to the clipboard.
map.内置 Unicode Emoji 数据集（含 CLDR 分组与多语言关键词），前: A built-in Unicode emoji dataset (with CLDR groups and multilingual keywords) filters in real time by keyword or category in the front end; clicking copies the emoji character or its code point (such as U+1F600). Complex emoji can be composed of
map.序列组合（如家庭、职业组合）。: sequences (families, profession combinations and so on).
map.数据随 Unicode 版本更新（15.x 已超 3000 个 Emoji）。: The dataset follows Unicode releases (15.x already has more than 3000 emoji).
map.纯前端本地检索，不上传；复制结果依赖系统字体回退渲染。: Search runs locally in the front end with nothing uploaded; how a copied emoji renders depends on system font fallback.
map.搜索关键词（中/英，如 笑 / fire / 爱心）: Search keyword (English or Chinese, e.g. laugh / fire / heart)
map.支持中英文关键词，按 emoji 名称与中文释义模糊匹配；留空显示全部。: English and Chinese keywords are supported, matched loosely against emoji names and Chinese glosses; leave it empty to show everything.
map.点击任意 emoji 即复制到剪贴板（兼容无 HTTPS/剪贴板 API 的环境: Click any emoji to copy it to the clipboard (the execCommand fallback covers environments without HTTPS or the Clipboard API).
map.内置约 180 个常用 emoji；更多字符建议用系统输入法的 emoji 面板: About 180 common emoji are built in; for anything beyond that, use the emoji panel of your system input method.
map.挑选并复制 Emoji 到文本。: Pick an emoji and copy it into your text.
map.给界面文案或社媒内容点缀表情：按分类浏览挑选，一键复制，不用记住码位。: Add a little personality to UI copy or social posts: browse by category, copy in one click, no need to remember code points.
map.码点一致，但各平台绘图形状不同。: The code points are identical, but each platform draws them differently.
map.该不该在正式文本里用 emoji？: Should emoji be used in formal text?
map.视场景而定。社媒与社区内容用 emoji 能提升亲和力；但合同、报错信息、技术文: It depends on the context. Emoji add warmth to social and community content, but be careful in contracts, error messages and technical documentation — platforms render them differently, screen readers read each one aloud, and some symbols are ambiguous. In formal text, keep the key information in words alone.
